slides.title: Semi-automatic photometer: operating modes (example of another instrument)
bullets: The manual describes a semi-automatic system using the automatic photometer Screen Master Plus (Hospitex) for biochemical tests; this is not the Mindray BA-88A — for Mindray follow the manufacturer’s manual.

A photometer measures light flux at fixed wavelengths: light passes a filter and is partly absorbed in the sample cuvette, a detector turns the light flux into an electrical signal and a microprocessor measures it.
The amount of light passing through the cuvette depends on the composition and amount of the substance in it.

Measuring modes of the example instrument: “end point” (with linear and non-linear calibration), “fixed time”, “kinetics” and multi-point calibration; bichromatic (two-wavelength) measurement is also possible.

slides.title: Semi-automatic photometer: operating modes (example of another instrument)
bullets: The instrument has several standard interference filters, a microcuvette and disposable cuvettes, and set temperature modes (25, 30 and 37 °C); many methods are pre-programmed.
Before a photometric test the instructions supplied with the test kit are read carefully.

slides.title: Instrument programming parameters and installation requirements (example)
bullets: Parameters entered when programming (example from the manual): method name, reaction type (end point, kinetics), zero (against reagent blank or water), unit, temperature, calibration mode, standard concentration, sample and reagent volumes, filter (wavelength), normal limits (maximum and minimum), linearity limit.
Calibration is done against a standard (calibrator) or by a factor; accuracy must be checked with control sera.
Calculation: by factor (optical density × factor) or by standard (sample optical density / standard optical density × standard concentration).
Placement: a clean room, a work bench with a hard surface, out of direct sunlight, free of vibration, on a horizontal surface.

slides.title: Instrument programming parameters and installation requirements (example)
bullets: The power cable is, if possible, connected separately from other instruments; the instrument should stand away from radio equipment and sources of strong electrical noise, and from air conditioners and heaters.
Read the manufacturer’s manual before using the instrument.

Technical characteristics of an automatic biochemical analyzer, installing the analyzer and its maintenance?
bullets: 1. Technical characteristics: type of analysis (discrete, random access), throughput (tests/hour), sample and reagent volume, photometer (wavelengths), ISE module, reaction cuvettes and incubation temperature (37 °C).
2. Installation: manufacturer's requirements – room temperature and humidity, stable power supply (UPS), water quality (deionized), space and ventilation; installation is done by an engineer.
3. Before putting into use: installation and operational tests, method verification, staff training.
4. Maintenance: daily (cleanliness of probe and cuvettes, reagents), weekly/monthly preventive maintenance schedule, calibration and controls.
5. Documentation: equipment log, faults and repairs, service contract; label a faulty analyzer and do not use it.

slides.title: Operating principles of an automatic biochemical analyzer. Programming a biochemical analyzer?
bullets: 1. Operating cycle: sample identification (barcode), dispensing sample and reagent, mixing, incubation at 37 °C, photometric measurement, calculation and transmission of the result to the LIS.
2. Measurement modes: end-point, two-point (fixed time), kinetic; bichromatic measurement; electrolytes by ISE.
3. Automatic functions: calibration, controls, automatic re-dilution (when out of range), hemolysis/lipemia/icterus indices, carry-over control.
4. Programming: entering test parameters (wavelength, volumes, time, calibrator values, linearity limit, units, reference intervals), control materials and rules.
5. After programming a new method – verification (precision, trueness, range) and documentation.

slides.title: Operating principles of a semi-automatic biochemical analyzer. Programming a biochemical analyzer?
bullets: 1. Semi-automatic analyzer: the operator prepares and mixes the sample and reagent manually, the analyzer aspirates, thermostats, measures and calculates.
2. Measurement modes: end-point, fixed time, kinetic; calculation by standard (factor).
3. Programming: test name, wavelength, temperature, aspiration volume, delay and measurement time, standard concentration or factor, linearity limit, units.
4. Sources of error: pipetting, mixing, timing, air bubbles, contamination of the flow cell and carry-over.
5. Quality: in each run a blank, calibrator and controls; daily cleaning and flushing.
